notes: Separate from research_sources.json: the earlier research record is preserved.
MORE definitions and relations are original design proposals pending Mati review; source terminology is not a domain mandate.
candidate.* identifiers identify documentary proposals only; they are not stable vocabulary IDs or Product Intelligence values.
described_period is the exhibition/event period, not inferred publication date; null publication_date means not established.
Historical style documentation is not evidence of current popularity, sales, available inventory or local adoption.
Public access does not grant image or content redistribution rights.

sources.title: Minimalism/Maximalism
sources.evidence: Contrasts reductive design with visual exuberance; minimalist design can use ornament to support construction.
limitations: Historical exhibition; contemporary wording refers to its exhibition period, not 2026.

sources.title: PUNK: Chaos to Couture
sources.evidence: Examines punk visual symbols and DIY themes including hardware, bricolage, graphics and deliberate destruction.
limitations: Does not define a universal visual classifier or prove current demand.

sources.title: Gothic: Dark Glamour
sources.evidence: Documents gothic themes across fashion and multiple historical/subcultural repertoires.
limitations: Black clothing alone is not a validated identification criterion; MORE domain choice remains proposed.

sources.title: Reinvention & Restlessness: Fashion in the Nineties
sources.evidence: Distinguishes grunge, minimalism, deconstruction and retro revival; describes grunge through layered, mismatched and worn-looking clothing.
limitations: Exhibition studies 1990s references; no date of manufacture inferred for a product.
An initially attempted /reinvention-restlessness/index.php URL failed; the listed fashion-in-the-nineties.php page was subsequently verified.

sources.title: Beyond Utility
sources.publisher: The Museum at FIT / FIT School of Graduate Studies
sources.evidence: Juxtaposes workwear, military and craft archetypes with fashion reinterpretations, separating visible codes from original functions.
limitations: Does not certify technical properties of any Mati product.

sources.title: Fresh, Fly, and Fabulous: Fifty Years of Hip Hop Style
sources.evidence: Documents the evolution and cultural specificity of hip hop fashion, including remixing and customization.
limitations: Hip hop is not treated as an exact synonym for all streetwear; identity of people is not inferred.

sources.title: Ivy Style
sources.evidence: Documents a collegiate repertoire and subsequent reinterpretations, including uses of the name preppy.
limitations: Partial relationship proposed by MORE; no universal equivalence of Ivy and preppy approved.

sources.title: Fashion in Motion: Saul Nash
sources.evidence: Describes a design practice reinterpreting sportswear and athleisure codes through movement and fashion.
limitations: Documents one practice rather than a universal athleisure definition or current market prevalence.

sources.title: Attire Guide: Dress Codes from Casual to White Tie
sources.evidence: Distinguishes event dress expectations, including black tie optional and creative black tie.
limitations: Cultural guidance is not a universal Bolivian norm; event instructions and Mati review remain necessary.

sources.title: Trend-ology
sources.evidence: Documents that fashion trends can emerge from changes in print, color, material, embellishment or silhouette and from diverse cultural sources.
limitations: Historical source is not a live trend measurement or approval of a new style.

sources.title: FAQ about Google Trends data
sources.evidence: Explains sampled, geographically and temporally normalized search interest, low-volume limits and why search spikes are not polling or sales evidence.
limitations: No trend queries, series or API integration executed.
The same normalized score between regions need not represent equal search volume.
